text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

An all-female panel is weak evidence on its own. In HR, risk and compliance functions, women are heavily represented, so a four-woman panel can easily arise by chance. Leading with it makes you look aggrieved rather than analytical, and it's the easiest part of your case to dismiss.

Your stronger ground is substantive: the credential gap, and the fact that a reasonable request for written reasons has gone unanswered for two weeks. Chase that in writing — politely, with a deadline — and ask for the scoring criteria and your scores against them.

Note that "broad regulatory experience" is genuinely valuable for a head of risk modelling: model approval and supervisory dialogue dominate the job. That may simply be the real reason.
